article.Citation: Agin-Liebes G, et al. Naturalistic Use of Mescaline Is Associated with Self-Reported Psychiatric Improvements and Enduring Positive Life Changes. ACS Pharmacology and Translational Science. 2021.
article.Title: Naturalistic Use of Mescaline Is Associated with Self-Reported Psychiatric Improvements and Enduring Positive Life Changes
article.GenderCategory: female 20%, male 76%, transgender or gender-fluid 4% (total sample, n=452)

ae_events.Description: Respondents reported very low rates of adverse experiences after mescaline use; no specific types, counts, or denominator given in this article
CEQ (Challenging Experiences Questionnaire) total-sample mean score 0.6 (SD 0.7) of 5, indicating low-intensity in-session challenging effects

article.IsObservational: Cross-sectional naturalistic online survey of self-selected mescaline users (author-described as 'cross-sectional study' in Discussion limitations); no randomization or investigator-administered intervention, so coded observational (Y).
article.Condition: Article analyzes five psychiatric/SUD subgroups (depression, anxiety, PTSD, alcohol misuse/AUD, drug misuse/DUD). Of the three condition options in scope for this review (Alcohol/Smoking/Opioid), only alcohol misuse/AUD is explicitly broken out as its own subgroup (n=72); DUD is a broad, non-opioid-specific drug-use category and smoking/nicotine is not addressed anywhere in the article, so 'Alcohol' is coded, though the study is not AUD-specific overall.
article.N: 452 is the final analyzed sample after excluding 22 respondents who could not specify mescaline type and 3 who were under 18 (from an initial 477 who completed the survey), so this is the final analyzed N, not merely enrolled/consented N.
article.ArmScope: Single-group naturalistic survey of mescaline users with no comparator arm or multi-arm structure; N, demographics, and the AE statement apply to the whole sample rather than one arm among several, so ArmScope is coded NA rather than psychedelic_arm/pooled.
article.AE_denominator: The article states only that 'respondents in our study reported very low rates of adverse experiences,' citing a companion report (Uthaug et al., under review, ref 18) using the same sample for the underlying detail; no explicit AE-specific denominator is given in this article's own text (the full N=452 is plausible but not stated for the AE assessment specifically), so coded not-reported.
article.PctIndigenous: Article discusses historical/traditional Indigenous (Native American Church) peyote use as background context but does not report what percentage of this survey's 452 respondents are Indigenous, so coded not-reported.
article.SafetyReported: The article contains one general sentence about AE rates for this same sample (see AE01), so safety is minimally addressed even though no specifics are given.
article.AnyAEReported: The cited sentence states adverse experiences did occur ('very low rates'), so AnyAEReported = Y rather than N or NA.
article.NumDistinctAEs: No specific AE types or a type-level count are given in this article (detail is deferred to a companion paper), matching the 'AEs reported but not counted' convention -> 'Not numbered'.
article.WorstSeverity: Equals the max severity across the two ae_events rows created from (1) the generic low-AE-rate statement and (2) the article's own quantitative CEQ challenging-experience data, both graded Mild.

ae_events.Agin-Liebes 2021_AE01: Graded on insufficient detail: the article gives no specific AE type, count, denominator, intervention, or outcome information, only a generic characterization as 'very low rates' with low overall harm risk (referencing a companion paper, ref 18, for detail not present in this text). Per the under-specified-AE rule, defaults to Mild with SeverityIndeterminate = Y.
ae_events.Agin-Liebes 2021_AE02: CEQ is the study's validated measure of expected in-session challenging-experience phenomenology; total-sample mean of 0.6/5 (SD 0.7) is low. Per the severity rubric, a low CEQ score defaults to Mild by intensity alone (not graded indeterminate, since the quantitative signal is clear and no intervention/persistence/seriousness signal is present). Reported as a separate 'challenging_experience' row rather than folded into the clinical 'AE' count, per the instruction to keep CEQ-sense phenomenology distinct.
